correctness.rationale: Starting K(t)=lambda E(e^{tJ}-1-tJ), fixed V=lambda(1+24q), the scale condition is exactly sup_{t>0} (1-1/M_q(t))/t; for t>=1/c, comparison Psi<=1/t prevents omission of the domain restriction. Power-series coefficients a_n=2[1+(5^{n+2}-1)q]/[(n+2)!(1+24q)] yield H=M(M-1)-tMprime. Exact b2,b3,b4 rational polynomials and roots were independently recomputed with SymPy. For n>=5, the jump-moment ratios and a1,a2>=3/4 (for q>=q_->1/50) imply b_n/a_n >= (3n^2-26n+86)/50>0, an infinite-coefficient proof. For q_-<=q<qc, H/t^3 has strictly positive derivative and opposite endpoint limits, so one interior optimum with negative second derivative. For qc<=q<=1, all b_n>=0 with b3>0, so strict decrease to the local third-cumulant boundary. Implicit-function theorem gives onset t_q=(b2prime/b3)(qc-q)+O((qc-q)^2), scale excess= (b2prime^2/2b3)(qc-q)^2+O((qc-q)^3). Independent symbolic computations reproduced qc=0.0563620637968 and slope 11.751349368; q=1/40 interior example is a supplementary numerical check.

value.rationale: Sub-gamma scale calibration is a natural sharp concentration invariant at a fixed true variance. A unique interior optimizer versus an endpoint regime changes which cumulant or finite tilt determines the best constant; resolving the precise q-critical transition and its quadratic onset matters for optimal concentration bounds and tests of the general variational principle. Not merely numerical reoptimization.
